newsitem.title: USA: Rochester Gas files competition plan.
newsitem.headline: Rochester Gas files competition plan.

text.p: Rochester Gas and Electric Corp said on Tuesday that it his filed a plan for opening electrical utility competition, that involves the company lowering electricity rates.

Under a proposed settlement, the company said it will continue to cut residential electricity rates through 2002 by five percent, as well as commercial and industrial rates by an average of 10 percent, Rochester Gas said.
Rochester Gas said residential customers will not pay for reductions for business customers.

The agreement with the staff of the New York Public Service Commission, large industrial customers and energy service companies provides for Rochester Gas to participate in existing and evolving energy markets through an unregulated subsidiary, Rochester Gas said.
Rochester Gas said the settlement will be open for public comment and must be approved by the New York State Public Service Commission. The company said it anticipates approval in June.

Rochester Gas said the proposed agreement will allow the company to recover past investments in large utility equipment, such as power generating plants. The company, however, said it does not guarantee full recovery on those investments.
The company was not immediately available for further comment about the utility's ability to recover investments in its equipment.
